# Changelog

## [1.91.277.0] - 2026-10-27

**office-hours stops carrying its own copy of the shared AskUserQuestion subsections.** After the shared-preamble hoist, office-hours still inlined whole copies of the shared `### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails` and `### Format` subsections, because each held one office-hours addition: the `Q<N>` open-question form. A session's first office-hours invocation read those subsections twice, once from the shared file and once from SKILL.md. The `Q<N>` form and its routing sentence now render as office-hours' own `### Open-ended questions` subsection at the end of the AskUserQuestion section, so the shared subsections apply as they are and office-hours' SKILL.md drops 6,328 bytes (its parity union goes from 160,952 to 154,624, under the pre-hoist 1.18 cap).

### Changed
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-ask-user-format.ts`**: office-hours' `Q<N>` form and "a free-text reply answers the most recent unanswered `Q<N>`" move into one `### Open-ended questions` subsection appended to the AskUserQuestion section. The form's template and Q-numbering text are unchanged; its lead-in now also carries what the Layout line used to say, "use this form instead of a `D<N>` brief" and the free-text routing rule. Other skills render byte-identically.
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble-hoist.ts`**: a skill variant may add subsections after the shared ones. It keeps only its changed and added subsections, and its note says "Only these subsections replace the shared ones or, under a new heading, add to its end". Variants without additions keep the existing note.
- **plan-eng-review keeps its versions** of the shared Tool resolution, fallback, Format, Self-check, Voice, plan-mode invocation and Plan Status Footer text, because each differs on purpose (the Scope gate, D-numbering after the target menu, the em-dash rule for composed prose, the selected-report footer, its own self-check). Its cap is unchanged.

### Tests
- `test/helpers/skill-startup.ts` applies added subsections when it builds the effective text, so the hoisted-equals-inline check covers office-hours' new layout. Its `scripts/harness-version.json` pin moves to the new blob, recorded non-behavioral at HARNESS_VERSION 6 with no pass-rate reset: `readSkillStartup`, `readSharedSections` and `readSkillEffective` return the same bytes as the pinned helper for every tier 2+ render without added subsections (735 across all hosts) and for office-hours' SKILL.md before this change, so office-hours' fixture input changes only because its prompt did.
- `test/preamble-hoist.test.ts` checks, on every host and tier, that a cut-down variant carries the "add to its end" note exactly when it adds a subsection, and that `readSkillEffective` puts a changed subsection in place and appends added ones in order.
- `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts`: office-hours' parity cap goes down from 1.2279 to 1.1796, its union as measured before the main merge (154,653 bytes; 154,624 now, 1.1793). After the v1.91.270.0 merge, `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` is recaptured and office-hours' ceiling goes down from 20,792 to 19,139. No cap or pin goes up.

### Gate integrity
- Corrections to the shared-preamble entry below: its post-v1.91.260.0 bullet should say the size allowlist carries 31 pin raises from #3433 and #3481 (23 and 8), not 30, and that `alwaysOnTotal` sits above main's unchanged ceiling (7,458) by the measured growth, so "all stay below main's pre-hoist values" holds for the per-skill rows only (`gstack` is back at main's 5,326 since the v1.91.265.0 merge). Its post-v1.91.265.0 bullet's "measured 7,542" for `alwaysOnTotal` is the raw bill; the ratchet's bill, which excludes test fixtures and aliases, measures 7,398.5 against the 7,542 ceiling. Its post-v1.91.270.0 bullet's "every row that rises matches main's own recapture" holds for the non-hoisted rows only (`alwaysOnTotal`, `capy/skill/gstack`, `diagram`, `gstack`, `gstack-upgrade`); the hoisted rows that rose (`eval-plan` 4,887, `landing-report`, `plan-tune`, `retro`, `ship`) are that branch's own recapture with main's growth included, and main measures them unhoisted (`eval-plan` 10,581).

## [1.91.276.0] - 2026-10-27

**Tier 2+ skills load the shared preamble once per session instead of once per invocation.** Every tier 2+ SKILL.md carried the same ~23 KB of preamble (AskUserQuestion format, voice, writing style, completeness, completion protocol and more), so each skill invocation re-read text the conversation already held. That text now renders once per host into `sections/preamble.md` beside each tier 2+ SKILL.md. The SKILL.md keeps a short "Shared preamble (load first)" pointer naming the file and its id (a hash of the shared text before host rewrites), and asks for the Read unless the skill's own earlier Read of that file, headed by that id, is still in context, so other text that merely carries the id cannot stand in for the shared rules. Measured with Anthropic token counting: review's SKILL.md drops from 21,884 to 16,103 tokens, ship from 22,688 to 16,907, office-hours from 27,100 to 23,085 and design-review from 39,040 to 33,261. The shared file is 5,953 tokens, so a skill's first invocation in a session costs about 170 tokens more than before (about 1,900 for office-hours, about 3,800 for plan-eng-review) and every later invocation of that skill saves about 5,800 (4,000 for office-hours, 2,200 for plan-eng-review). The skip is tied to the skill's own copy of the file, so the first invocation of each different skill pays the Read again. A /autoplan run's four review-skill loads carry 17,941 fewer SKILL.md tokens (191,871 → 173,930), and /autoplan and the inline /office-hours loader skip each loaded skill's "Shared preamble (load first)" section, because the parent already holds the shared preamble.

### Changed
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble-hoist.ts`** (new) renders `{{PREAMBLE}}` for tier 2+ skills: a section moves to the shared file only when this skill's render of it is byte-identical to the shared render, so no skill's instructions change. Sections that name the skill (the start command, Question Tuning, Repo Ownership, Search Before Building, Telemetry), text without its own heading, and skill-specific variants stay inline; a variant that keeps the shared subsection headings carries only its differing `###` subsections. Tier 1 skills keep their short preamble inline. Across all 41 hoisted skills, the SKILL.md with its shared file applied holds exactly the paragraphs the pre-hoist SKILL.md held.
- **`scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts`** emits `sections/preamble.md` per tier 2+ skill and host as a new `preamble` artifact kind, with the same host rewrites, install-root rewrite and runtime preludes as SKILL.md. `setup` already installs every skill's `sections/`, and gstack-built overlay and per-install renders carry the file the same way.
- **`setup --status`**: a bare `sections/<file>` pointer counts as carved only when the skill installs a section other than the shared `preamble.md`, so the new file does not turn on checks for skills that inline their sections on that host.
- **`gstack-doctor --check`**: the `patch` row finds the Codex render's model patch in the review skill's `sections/preamble.md` too, where the hoist moves it; without this the required row failed on every hoisted Codex install.
- **Loaded-skill skip lists** (`/autoplan`'s section skip list and the `{{INVOKE_SKILL}}` loader's defaults in `scripts/resolvers/composition.ts`) skip `Shared preamble (load first)`, so a loaded plan-review or /office-hours skill no longer Reads its own shared file and re-imports the sections the parent already handles. `Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean` and `Completion Status Protocol` leave both lists, because no loaded skill carries them inline any more, only in the shared file. Each list is 40 characters shorter, so 30 size pins go down (plan-eng-review's by 26, after main's +14 pointer growth).
- **PR paid planner** (`scripts/lib/paid-select.ts`): a generated `<skill>/sections/preamble.md` takes its skill's `SKILL.md.tmpl` identity, as that skill's SKILL.md already does, so a skill whose only paid coverage is periodic defers it instead of failing `screen-summary` with "requires full validation".

- `test/helpers/skill-startup.ts` (new): `readSkillStartup` (SKILL.md with the shared file spliced in at its pointer, the reading order a skill sees) and `readSkillEffective` (each preamble section once, with this skill's variant applied). Tests that assert preamble rules are in context, E2E fixture extractors, workflow-judge bundles and install checks read these instead of SKILL.md alone; judge bundles keep their pre-hoist content.
- `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts`: parity caps for ship, review, autoplan, spec, land-and-deploy, design-consultation, plan-devex-review, plan-ceo-review, office-hours and plan-eng-review raised to their measured unions (owner-approved, Garry 2026-10-25: "do it"), each with its reason. The existing TS2769 test-typecheck baseline entry for `test/gen-skill-docs-checks.test.ts` is re-keyed for the new `preamble` artifact kind, its count unchanged.

**The Completeness Principle now asks for complete coverage with minimal code.** Every tier-2+ skill's preamble said "the complete thing is the goal", and ETHOS.md told models to "always prefer A" because "the 70-line delta costs seconds". Models read that as permission to write more code, which is the "50-line job arriving as 400" complaint (GSTA-93). Coverage of the requirement is still non-negotiable; code beyond it is no longer a virtue.

### Changed
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-completeness-section.ts`**: the default section reads "Complete coverage, minimal code": recommend full coverage of the requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) and no code beyond it, prefer the smaller diff at equal coverage, and add no checks for impossible states. Unrelated work stays separate scope. The `Completeness: X/10` scoring rule and the GPT-5.6 Sol variant are unchanged. The section is 3 characters shorter, so every regenerated skill shrinks and 89 size pins go down.
- **`ETHOS.md`**: "Completeness is cheap ... always prefer A" becomes "Complete coverage, minimal code": completeness is measured in coverage, not lines; at equal coverage choose the smaller diff; no speculative abstractions, impossible-state checks or unneeded refactors. A new anti-pattern names the impossible-state fallback. Section 1's opener now says "When covering the whole requirement costs minutes more than the shortcut, cover it. Every time. Complete means complete coverage, not more code.", and "How They Work Together" says Boil the Ocean means "cover the whole requirement with the least code" instead of "do the complete thing".
- **`plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md.tmpl`**: the Philosophy bullet "COMPLETENESS IS CHEAP: AI makes 70 LOC seconds. Prefer complete ~150 LOC over 90% ~80 LOC. Boil the ocean." becomes "COMPLETENESS IS COVERAGE": cover the whole requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) rather than a 90% shortcut, add no code beyond the accepted scope (so SCOPE EXPANSION and SELECTIVE EXPANSION still build what the user accepted), and choose the smaller diff at equal coverage. plan-ceo-review is under the 100,000-character limit on every host and has no size pin, so it grows about 100 characters without a pin change.
- **First-run intro**: the one-time Boil the Ocean intro in `bin/gstack-skill-start` says "complete coverage, minimal code" instead of "do the complete thing when AI makes marginal cost near-zero". The agents digest's Boil the Ocean bullet (`scripts/gen-agents-digest.ts`, regenerated `agents-digest/gstack-AGENTS.md`) says the same: "complete coverage, minimal code: cover the whole requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) and write no code beyond it".
- `review/specialists/simplification.md` quotes the new house rule instead of "If A is 70 lines more, choose A", and `CLAUDE.md` restates it in place of "Completeness is cheap ... the complete thing is the goal".

### Tests
- `test/model-overlays.test.ts` asserts the new default wording ("Complete coverage, minimal code.", "prefer the smaller diff") and checks, one sentence per rule, that the section still states full coverage of the requirement with no code beyond it, the smaller diff only at equal coverage, no checks for impossible states, and that unrelated work is separate scope that never excuses a gap.
- `test/ceo-workflow-clarity.test.ts` checks that the plan-ceo-review Philosophy bullet still asks for the whole requirement over a 90% shortcut, no code beyond the accepted scope and the smaller diff at equal coverage, and that "COMPLETENESS IS CHEAP" and "~150 LOC" stay gone.
- `test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts` checks that the house rule `review/specialists/simplification.md` quotes is still stated in ETHOS.md. `test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts` checks that the first-run intro says complete coverage, minimal code and never "do the complete thing".
- `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json`: 89 pins lowered by 3 characters each. None raised; the plan-ceo-review rewording touches no pinned skill.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, budget, timeout, trial count, case kind or assertion weakened. The section heading "Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean" is unchanged.

## [1.91.275.0] - 2026-10-27

### Changed
- **Policy key versions are stamped, not hand-moved** (`lib/ship-policy.ts`, `.gstack/ship-policy.json`): `DOCS_CAPS_KEY_VERSION` is 1.91.270.0, the release that shipped `docs.caps` (#3487 was written naming 1.91.258.0, which main stamped for another PR; a slot call never permits an edit beyond the four stamp files, so the constant could not move at the slot). gstack's own policy now lists `lib/ship-policy.ts` under `stamp_paths` with the `_KEY_VERSION = '{version}'` template in `stamp_patterns`: a new key's constant is written as a tentative future version clear of main's pace (the next minor) and `gstack-restamp`'s stamp_paths stage moves it to the allocated version at the slot stamp, reading the base branch's policy, so the stage is live for the PRs after this one; the tree receipt's stamp-only check still accepts that move only when the tentative value equals the base version at the slot, so a PR that adds a key cannot clear the train until #3512 lands. `test/gstack-ship-policy.test.ts` adds the check the incident lacked: a released key's version must be a CHANGELOG heading whose entry names the key, so a tentative value no stamp moved fails (keys from before `review_scope` are exempt).

## [1.91.274.0] - 2026-10-27

**/design-html and /design-review now run the design lint, and its copy tier reports every content and ship-floor tell at its line (hallmark phase 2, GSTA-92; Garry 2026-10-26 "Do it", option a).** The two design skills still called `gstack-design-craft`, which counted tells without positions and kept accepted exceptions in finalized.json. The lint already carried the same ids, so the skills now call it, the copy tier has its own patterns with line numbers, and a page answers a tell with a waiver comment beside it instead of a side record.

### Changed
- **/design-html** Step 4 runs `gstack-design-lint <page> --render` after the Slop Gate and reads its exit code: 2 fixes every `blocks` line, 1 fixes or waives each `ask` line, 0 lists `polish` as notes. A missing `LINT_SUMMARY`, a `render` line or `render=skipped` is said plainly and the static lines stand.
- **Waivers live in the page.** A real customer named Nexus or a supplied 50% figure gets `<!-- gstack-lint-disable <rule-id>: <reason about this page, 24+ chars> -->`, written only for what the user supplied or confirmed. This supersedes #3422's persisted craft exceptions: `--accepted` and finalized.json's `craft_exceptions` are gone, and the hand-off lists every waiver.
- **Copy-tier tiers**: `placeholder-name`, `placeholder-brand`, `lorem`, `round-number` and `needs-proof` move from blocks to ask, so the waiver above can answer them. /design-review still files a waived `needs-proof` or `lorem`, which a live page cannot carry.
- **/design-review's craft audit** runs the lint on each saved page: `blocks` and `ask` lines are category 9 findings at their line, `waived` lines are listed with their reason, `empty-mount-node` sends the audit to the saved DOM. A saved live page has lost its linked CSS, so the audit files only its copy-tier (`craft`) lines there and judges the CSS rules by eye.
- **`lib/design-lint/rules/copy.ts`** holds the copy tier's own patterns (moved from `lib/design-craft.ts`), reporting each tell at its line with what matched. It reads visible text, script bodies and inline handlers (single-quoted included) and the parsed tags, so a hydration payload, commented-out markup or a `<title>` string inside a script no longer counts.

### Added
- **`empty-mount-node`** (ask, page only): a body with no text, a `<noscript>` notice aside, that loads a script is a client-rendered shell; the lint says it read none of its content instead of passing it.

### Removed
- `bin/gstack-design-craft`, `lib/design-craft.ts` and `test/design-craft.test.ts`. Their checks are in the lint's copy tier and its tests; the archetype handoff tests moved to `test/design-craft-resolvers.test.ts`.

### Tests
- `test/design-lint.test.ts`: the copy tier at its lines with the catalog's fixes, the clean page with inlined Pretext, the skip link and `aria-current`, visible-text reading, the four checker limits #3433 documented, and the shell check (noscript, image-only page, component scope). `test/design-lint-recorded.test.ts` reads the recorded page's buzzwords at lines 32 and 37.
- The `design-html-slop-gate` paid case looks for a `gstack-design-lint` call, and its touchfiles select on `lib/design-lint/**` and `bin/gstack-design-lint`.
